claim: For the 3-uniform hypergraph \(F_5\) with edges \(\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\},\{c,d,e\}\) on five distinct vertices, every \(F_5\)-free 3-uniform hypergraph on six vertices has at most \(10\) edges, with equality if and only if it consists of all triples containing one fixed vertex; hence \(\operatorname{ex}_3(6,F_5)=10\) and the six labeled extremizers form one isomorphism class.

limitations: No assertion for other vertex counts.
The original 1983 source full text was not inspected, so historical priority for the finite case remains uncertain.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.method: Complete enumeration of all \(2^{20}\) labeled hypergraphs, with 180 distinct forbidden masks and all \(720\) relabelings used for extremizer canonicalization.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.reproducibility: Standalone C++17 verifier is embedded as verify_f5_n6.cpp.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Exact statement for simple 3-uniform hypergraphs on six vertices only.

title: The six-vertex Turán extremum for \(F_5\)
